'''Alina Anca von Davier''' (born September 11, 1967) is a psychometrician and researcher in [[computational psychometrics]], machine learning, and education. Von Davier is a researcher, innovator, and an executive leader with over 20 years of experience in EdTech and in the assessment industry. She is the Chief of Assessment at [[Duolingo]], where she leads the [[Duolingo English Test]] research and development area. She is also the Founder and CEO of EdAstra Tech, a service-oriented EdTech company. In 2022, she joined the [[University of Oxford]] as an Honorary Research Fellow,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.education.ox.ac.uk/people/alina-von-davier/|title=Dr Alina von Davier|access-date=2023-02-13}}</ref> and [[Carnegie Mellon University]] as a Senior Research Fellow.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cmu.edu/dietrich/news/news-stories/2022/november/ml-vondavier.html|title=Duolingo's Alina von Davier joins the Department of Modern Languages|access-date=2023-02-13}}</ref>

== Education ==
Von Davier completed a M.S. in Mathematics from the [[University of Bucharest]] in 1990. In 2000, she earned a doctorate in mathematics from [[Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mathopt.de/PUBLICATIONS/festschriftMathe.pdf|title=Universität Magdeburg, Institut für Mathematische Optimierung|access-date=2020-06-12}}</ref> In 2019 she completed classes in an Executive MBA program at [[Harvard Business School]].

==Career==
As one of the pioneers of the field of computational psychometrics, von Davier has dedicated her career to advancing the field through her work in both academia and industry. She served as Chief Officer at [[ACT (test)]] leading ACTNext, an R&D-based innovation division. Prior to this, she worked for 15 years at [[Educational Testing Service]], where her latest position was Senior Center Director. In 2020, she left her position at ACT and joined [[Duolingo]] as Chief of Assessment for the [[Duolingo English Test]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thepienews.com/newmove/alina-von-davier/|title=New Move: Alina von Davier {{!}} The PIE News|website=www.thepienews.com|date=14 August 2020 |access-date=2021-10-23}}</ref>

Von Davier has made significant contributions to the field of psychometrics through her work in academic settings. She was the Chair of the Editorial Council of the [[Psychometric Society]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.psychometricsociety.org/content/editorial-council|title=Editorial Council {{!}} Psychometric Society|website=www.psychometricsociety.org|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref> and an associate editor of [[Psychometrika]]. She also served as guest editor for both [[Applied Psychological Measurement]] and the [[Journal of Educational Measurement]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=von Davier |first1=Alina A. |last2=Liu |first2=Mei |title= Special Issue |journal=Applied Psychological Measurement |date=January 2008 |volume=32 |issue=1 |pages=1–114 |url=https://journals.sagepub.com/toc/apma/32/1 |issn=0146-6216}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=von Davier |first1=Alina A. |title=Special Issue: Collaborative Educational Assessments |journal=Journal of Educational Measurement |date=2017 |volume=54 |issue=1 |pages=1–141 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/toc/17453984/2017/54/1 |issn=1745-3984}}</ref> In 2022 she served as the Chairperson of the global board of directors for the [[Association of Test Publishers]], and was the president of the International Association of Computerized Adaptive Testing from 2019 to 2022.

Von Davier was a member of the Board of Directors for [[Smart Sparrow]], an adaptive learning company from 2018 to 2020. She currently serves as a Director on the Board for MACAT, an education company focused on critical and creative thinking, learning and assessment.

She currently sits on the global board of directors for the [[Association of Test Publishers]] and is the president of the International Association of Computerized Adaptive Testing.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.iacat.org/content/current-iacat-board|title=Current IACAT Board {{!}} IACAT|website=www.iacat.org|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref>

== Recognition ==
Von Davier’s work has been widely recognized in the academic community. In 2019, she was a finalist for the Innovator award from the EdTech Digest.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.edtechdigest.com/2019-finalists-winners/|title=2019 Award Winners{{!}} EdTech Digest|website=www.edtechdigest.com|access-date=2023-02-13}}</ref> In 2020, she received ATP’s Career Award for her contributions to assessment.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://atpu.memberclicks.net/atp-2020-awards-winners|title=2020 ATP Award Winners{{!}} ATP|website=www.atpu.org|access-date=2023-02-13}}</ref> The [[American Educational Research Association]] awarded her the Division D Signification Contribution Educational Measurement and Research Methodology Award for her publications “Computerized Multistage Testing: Theory and Applications” (2014) and an edited volume on test equating, “Statistical Models for Test Equating, Scaling, and Linking” (2011).<ref>{{Cite press release|url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/alina-von-davier-honored-at-2013-american-educational-research-association-annual-meeting-206737281.html|title=Alina von Davier Honored at 2013 American Educational Research Association Annual Meeting{{!}} PR Newswire|website=www.prnewswire.com|access-date=2023-02-13}}</ref> In 2022 she received the [[National Council on Measurement in Education]]'s Bradley Hanson award for her work on adaptive testing and for the co-authored  book on computer adaptive testing with R.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ncme.org/about/awards/ncme-awards/bradley-hanson|title=2022 NCME Awards {{!}} NCME|website=www.NCME.org|access-date=2023-02-13}}</ref>

== Selected works ==

=== Books and edited volumes ===
* von Davier, A. A., Mislevy, R.J., and Hao, J. (Eds.) (2021). ''Computational Psychometrics: New Methodologies for a New Generation of Digital Learning and Assessment: With Examples in R and Python (Methodology of Educational Measurement and Assessment).'' Springer International Publishing.
* von Davier, A.A. (2017). Measurement issues in collaborative learning and assessment. [Special Issue]. ''Journal of Educational Measurement, 54(1).''
* von Davier, A.A., Zhu, M., and Kyllonen, P.C. (2017). ''Innovative Assessment of Collaboration''. Springer International Publishing.
* Yan, D., von Davier, A. A., and Lewis, C. (Eds.) (2014). ''Computerized multistage testing: Theory and applications''. London, UK: Chapman & Hall.
* Mislevy, R. J., Corrigan, S., Oranje, A., Dicerbo, K., John, M., Bauer, M. I., Hoffman, E., von Davier, A. A., and Hao, J. (2014), ''Psychometrics and game-based assessments''. [https://www.instituteofplay.org/ Institute of Play].
* von Davier, A. A. (Ed.) (2011). ''Statistical models for test equating, scaling and linking.'' New York, NY: Springer-Verlag.
* von Davier, A. A., and Liu, M. (Eds.) (2008). Population Invariance of Test Equating and Linking: Theory Extension and Applications Across Exams [Special Issue]. ''Applied Psychological Measurement, 32''(1).
* von Davier, A. A., Holland, P. W., and Thayer, D. T. (2004). ''The kernel method of test equating.'' New York, NY: Springer Verlag.
* von Davier, A. A. (2001). ''Testing unconfoundedness in regression models with normally distributed regressors'' [Dissertation]. Aachen, Germany: Shaker Verlag.
